title: Perfect-source derived Hom with a relatively flat coefficient commutes with arbitrary base change
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Quasi-coherent modules are as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and ordinary tensor pullback and direct image are [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived pullback uses K-flat resolutions with flat terms and derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. A perfect object is etale locally isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated: every affine scheme base change of $f$ has quasi-compact source, and its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. A space is quasi-compact when it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme. Let $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be perfect, and let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $Y$, meaning stalkwise flat over the base local rings on compatible etale scheme charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Regard $M$ as a complex in degree zero. For any morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ of algebraic spaces, put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. With derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the canonical base-change comparison is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{Y'})$:
$$Lg^*Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(P,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{X'}}(Lh^*P,h^*M).$$
The coefficient on the right is ordinary tensor pullback, not derived pullback. The comparison is the canonical derived direct-image base-change map followed by the internal-Hom pullback comparison and the map induced by $Lh^*M\to h^*M$. It is natural in $P,M$ and in base change. No properness, Noetherian, coherence or finiteness hypothesis on $M$ or $g$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08JQ (lemma-base-change-RHom), case (1), with the relatively flat complex concentrated in degree zero; canonical map in the first paragraph of its proof.

proof.text: Put $M'=h^*M$ and $\phi:Lh^*(M[0])\to M'[0]$, the canonical derived-to-ordinary tensor pullback comparison. Ordinary tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence by the cited module theorem. Thus $K=M[0]$ and $K'=M'[0]$ belong to their respective quasi-coherent derived subcategories; their only possible cohomology is in degree zero.

source.place: 08JQ proof: coefficient pair; 0A1K proof: derived-to-ordinary comparison.

proof.text:
Check the stalk condition for $\phi$ using the etale-chart criterion. On any of its scheme squares $U'=U\times_V V'$, write $N$ for the Zariski quasi-coherent module with $\epsilon_U^*N=M|_U$. The derived etale-Zariski equivalence and its pullback comparison $\epsilon_{U'}^*Lh_U^*\simeq Lh_{U,\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_U^*$, together with the pullback composition comparison for $U'\to X'\to X$ equal to $U'\to U\to X$, identify the transported coefficient map $\phi_U$ with the Zariski derived-to-ordinary comparison $Lh_U^*N\to h_U^*N$: both are the canonical map to $H^0$ of the same derived pullback, ordinary pullback being right exact. Fix $z\in U'$ with images $x\in U$, $v'\in V'$, $v\in V$. Set $R=\mathcal O_{V,v}$, $A=\mathcal O_{U,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{V',v'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{U',z}$. The hypothesis on $M$ and the relative-flat stalk theorem give $N_x$ flat over $R$. The bounded-flat K-flat theorem applied to $N_x[0]$ makes $N_x\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B$ represented by $(N_x\otimes_R B)[0]$. The module pullback-stalk theorem identifies $(h_U^*N)_z$ with $N_x\otimes_A C$, with the unit sending $n$ to $n\otimes1$. For $i\ne0$ both sides of the chart comparison are zero. For $i=0$ that comparison is
$$(N_x\otimes_R B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C\longrightarrow N_x\otimes_A C,\quad(n\otimes b)\otimes c\longmapsto n\otimes bc.$$
Its inverse is $n\otimes c\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes c$; balancing verifies both composites are identities. These are the canonical maps, since $\phi$ is the derived-to-ordinary comparison and the stalk unit has the specified formula. The chart criterion now gives the geometric stalk condition for $\phi$ everywhere. No flatness of $A$ or $B$ over $R$ was used.

source.place: 08JQ final sentence, referring to the stalk computation in 0A1K; 0DKG chart equivalence.

proof.text:
Apply perfect-source internal-Hom inheritance to $K=M[0]$, $K'=M'[0]$, $\phi$ and the given perfect $P$. Steps 1 and 2 check its quasi-coherence and stalk hypotheses. It gives quasi-coherent $J=R\mathcal Hom(P,M)$ and $J'=R\mathcal Hom(Lh^*P,M')$, and proves the stalk condition for
$$\psi:Lh^*J\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom(Lh^*P,Lh^*M)\longrightarrow J'.$$
The first arrow is the evaluation transpose and the second is induced by $\phi$. This inheritance theorem imposes no boundedness on $K,K'$ and no flatness of the square.

source.place: 08JQ proof: apply 0DKI(2) to the coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Apply the single-complex base-change theorem to $J,J',\psi$. Their quasi-coherence and all their stalk comparisons were verified in step 3; $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by hypothesis. It follows that $Lg^*Rf_*J\to Rf'_*Lh^*J\xrightarrow{Rf'_*(\psi)}Rf'_*J'$ is an isomorphism. Its first arrow is the theorem's pulled-counit adjunction mate. The formula for $\psi$ in step 3 is exactly internal-Hom pullback followed by the map induced by $Lh^*M\to h^*M$. Therefore this is the comparison in the statement, with ordinary coefficient pullback on the right.

For naturality in $P$ and $M$, use naturality of the evaluation-transpose comparison and of $\phi$; the pulled-counit exchange is a natural transformation, so composing these squares gives the asserted square after $Rf'_*$. For a further base morphism $t:Y''\to Y'$, transpose the two composites under the pullback/direct-image adjunctions. The cited monoidal comparisons give the pullback composition comparisons $c$, their compatibility with the tensor comparisons, and the counit of a composite adjunction as the composite of the pulled counits. Hence the exchange of the pasted square is the pasting of the two exchanges, the evaluation transposes compose, and both transposes are the pullback of the same counit, followed by the same evaluation and the ordinary coefficient map, after $c$ identifies their sources. The adjunction bijection makes the composites equal. Identity base change gives the unit triangle identity. This verifies naturality of the specified comparison, without requiring that $Lh^*M\to h^*M$ itself be an isomorphism.

source.place: 08JQ canonical-map paragraph; 0DKI proof, the two-arrow evaluation comparison.
